newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa surgery averted fatal heart attack.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa surgery averted fatal heart attack.

text.p: Mother Teresa had successful surgery on Friday to clear coronary artery blockages that would have triggered a fatal heart attack if not treated, an American member of her medical team said.
Doctor Patricia Aubanel said some danger remained to the 86-year-old Roman Catholic missionary's heart and it would take her up to three months to recover.
It was the third time in five years that Mother Teresa, known as the "Saint of the Gutters" for her devotion to the poor, had undergone angiography and angioplasty.
"She was going to have a heart attack -- a major heart attack -- if the angioplasty was not done," Aubanel told reporters at the B.M. Birla Heart Research centre in Calcutta.
"Mother could not have left the hospital alive without this angioplasty," added Aubanel, who treated Mother Teresa in California in 1991.
A medical bulletin said the surgical procedure was successful. "Mother at present is in stable condition. However, she is still not out of risk," it said.
"Many complications can still arise and her irregular heart rhythm still continues to be a problem," the bulletin added.
Dr D.P. Shetty, who led the surgical team, said angioplasty could be repeated, if necessary.
"We were fully prepared and in case of an emergency we are ready for surgery. I was sure she would recover, although statistically the risks are very high," he said.
Angiography is an X-ray test which uses an injected opaque dye to show up blocked arteries. Angioplasty is the procedure to unblock the artery by inserting a balloon and inflating it.
The procedures were performed eight days after Mother Teresa, the 1979 Nobel Peace Prize winner, entered hospital with an irregular heartbeat. She was fitted with a pacemaker in 1979.
The medical bulletin said the angiogram revealed "blockages in the two major coronary arteries".
"The (medical) panel then decided to proceed to perform angioplasty, which was performed successfully in these two vessels," it added.
It was the third time Mother Teresa had had coronary angiography and angioplasty. The others were performed in the United States in 1991 and at the Birla centre in 1993.
"I heard that she came out of the operation theatre smiling and doctors congratulated her," Sister Prasanna, a member of Mother Teresa's Missionaries of Charity, told Reuters.
Aubanel said: "She surprises everybody. She has amazing records of speedy recovery. At least on four earlier occasions she was nearly dead, but every time she recovered.
"Absolutely amazing at her age. She has spiritual strength. We hope she will recover this time. We never had a problem to convince her that she needed angioplasty.
"We will have to keep her under close watch for the next 24 hours. Mother has coronary disease, hypertension and cholesterol which can be dealt with properly," she added.
In a medical bulletin several hours before the procedures, doctors said Mother Teresa's condition had improved and she had gone 24 hours without chest pains.
Doctors said she had suffered heart failure several times since entering the Woodlands Nursing Home in Calcutta on November 22. She was moved to the Birla clinic on Tuesday.
Throughout her stay in hospital, members of the Missionaries of Charity, which has about 4,500 nuns in some 80 countries and was founded by Mother Teresa in 1949, prayed for her recovery.
